questionText: Consider allocation of memory to a new process. Assume that none of the existing holes in the memory will exactly fit the process's memory requirement. Hence, a new hole of smaller size will be created if allocation is made in any of the existing holes. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: The hole created by worst fit is always larger than the hole created by best fit.
The hole created by worst fit is always larger than the hole created by first fit.
The hole created by best fit is never larger than the hole created by first fit.
The hole created by next fit is never larger than the hole created by best fit.
explanation:
Step 1: Understand Memory Allocation Strategies
Let $P$ be the memory size requested by the process.
When a process of size $P$ is allocated inside a hole of size $H$ ($H > P$), the size of the newly created hole is $(H - P)$.

Step 2: Analyze Best Fit vs First Fit
• Best Fit selects the smallest hole that is large enough to fit the process.
• Let $H_{best}$ be the hole selected by Best Fit and $H_{first}$ be the hole selected by First Fit.
• By definition of Best Fit, $H_{best} \le H_{first}$.
• Subtracting $P$ from both sides gives: $(H_{best} - P) \le (H_{first} - P)$.
• Hence, the hole created by Best Fit is never larger than the hole created by First Fit. This makes statement (C) TRUE.

Step 3: Analyze Other Options
• Option A: If all valid holes are of equal size, Worst Fit and Best Fit will choose holes of equal size, making the remaining hole sizes equal (not strictly larger).
• Option B: If First Fit happens to scan and pick the largest hole, the remaining hole created by First Fit will equal that of Worst Fit.
• Option D: Next Fit can pick a hole larger than Best Fit, creating a larger remaining hole.
